newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht steady, interbank rate lower late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht steady, interbank rate lower late.

text.p: The Thai baht held steady in late thin trade in the domestic market as the market did not react to central bank monthly economic data which showed sharply lower foreign reserves, dealers said.
"The volume is very thin. The economic figures did not contain any major surprise," a dealer at a foreign bank.
The baht was quoted at 25.850/25.900 to the dollar late against 25.800/25.900 in the early morning.
Dealers said the sharply smaller foreign reserves did not have significant impact on the baht as the figure was in line with market expectation.
"The market expected foreign reserves to drop after the central bank's aggressive intervention last month. The figure is not so bad," said another dealer.
The Bank of Thailand said on Thursday foreign reserves fell to $33.3 billion at end-May from $37.3 billion in the previous month.
The central bank attributed the sharp reserve decline to its intervention to defend the baht after it faced speculative attack last month.
In the offshore market, the baht eased to 25.450/25.650 late from 25.300/25.400 in the morning.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was at 45/75 satangs per dollar offshore and 20/25 in the local market.
The overnight interbank rate eased further to 15-16 percent in late trade from 16-17 earlier on rising liquidity and some money inflows, dealers said.
"Liquidity rose today. There was also increasing amount of foreing funds in non-resident accounts. They may park here before entering the stock market," said a money market dealer.
Thai stocks soared 4.84 percent at the Thursday close as foreign investors began putting money back into the bourse by buying cheap blue chip bank and communications issues, brokers said.
